what: Hand labels, per turn, for DISMISSAL (explicitly declining to weigh a concern that belongs to someone else) and ACCOMMODATION (conceding ground to, or aligning with, another participant) on SONNET 5 output at 15 turns — the re-validation the backlog required before any Sonnet rate is compared to a Haiku one.
why: ACCOMMODATION and DISMISSAL in scripts/score_validation.py were validated against Haiku 4.5 at 15 turns; the default model is now Sonnet 5.
labeller: assistant, reading every full turn BEFORE running the patterns; borderline cases recorded as 'soft' and not counted in the hand rate

result.patch: Patterns added to ACCOMMODATION (8) and DISMISSAL (4) in scripts/score_validation.py, written against runs 327167c9 and 486c6dbb only.

result.finding: Before the patch the lists made arm B and arm D look alike on dismissal (0.167 vs 0.133) and showed NO accommodation on Sonnet at all. By hand the B-vs-D dismissal gap is large and in the same direction as on Haiku (0.467 vs 0.167 here; 0.400 vs 0.200 on Haiku), and arm D accommodates more than arm B (0.233 vs 0.100). No Sonnet rate computed with the pre-patch lists should be quoted.
